interest: It shows how SCAP and the US channeled Japanese, Korean and Ryukyu drug data and laws to international bodies. It includes full regulations, statistics and peace-treaty debate.
overview: This 277-page State Department file (August 1947–December 1949) documents Occupied Japan's narcotics control and international reporting. It holds SCAP, Korean and Ryukyu statistical returns, Japanese drug laws and regulations, UN questionnaire replies and annual reports. It also contains Treasury, UN and Permanent Central Opium Board correspondence, and late-1949 telegrams on dropping a narcotics article from the peace treaty.
